name: SQL (SQLite)
summary: Learn SQL queries, joins, grouping, transactions, and indexes with local SQLite.

prerequisites: Know how to open a terminal and save a plain text file.
Use the sqlite3 CLI or a local SQLite client. Run each example in a fresh in-memory database unless the exercise says otherwise.
metadata.miniProject: Build a study-log database with topics and attempts. Add foreign keys and a nonnegative duration check. Query per-topic totals and recent attempts, then test rejected inserts, an empty topic, and transaction rollback.

lessons.title: Tables, constraints, and inserts
lessons.explanation: A table gives columns names and type affinities. Define keys and constraints to protect invariants. Examples in this pack can run separately in a new in-memory SQLite database. To run a file in a terminal, use sqlite3 :memory: < lesson.sql. This opens a fresh disposable database. The default CLI separates output columns with vertical bars.

api.name: CREATE TABLE
api.description: Declare a table and its columns.

api.name: PRIMARY KEY
api.description: Identify a row uniquely.

api.name: INSERT INTO ... VALUES
api.description: Add one or more rows.

api.name: CHECK (...)
api.description: Reject values that violate a column or row condition.

lessons.practice: Add a third topic. Try inserting negative minutes and a duplicate title.
lessons.pitfall: Column affinity is different from strict type enforcement in an ordinary SQLite table.

exercise.expected: Insert a valid third topic, then try a duplicate title and a negative duration in separate statements.
exercise.completion: Both invalid rows are rejected and the valid row appears in the query.

lessons.title: Filtering, sorting, and missing values
lessons.explanation: SELECT chooses output expressions. WHERE filters rows, and ORDER BY specifies output order. NULL represents an absent value and has its own predicates.
lessons.example:
WITH scores(name, points) AS (
    VALUES ('Ari', 8), ('Bea', NULL), ('Casey', 9), ('Dev', 4)
)
SELECT name, COALESCE(points, 0) AS shown_points
FROM scores
WHERE points >= 8 OR points IS NULL
ORDER BY shown_points DESC, name
LIMIT 3;

api.name: WHERE condition
api.description: Keep rows for which the condition is true.

api.name: IS NULL / IS NOT NULL
api.description: Test for an absent or present value.

api.name: COALESCE(a, b)
api.description: Return the first non-NULL value.

api.name: ORDER BY ... LIMIT ...
api.description: Sort results and cap the number returned.

lessons.practice: Show only rows with a real score. Sort them by points, then name.
lessons.pitfall: Use IS NULL for missing values. The expression points = NULL does not evaluate to true.

exercise.expected: Show only real scores and use a predictable ordering.
exercise.completion: NULL scores are excluded and equal scores are ordered by name.

lessons.title: Relationships and joins
lessons.explanation: Join tables by matching related keys. An inner join includes only matching pairs. A left join also keeps rows from its left input that have no match and fills the right columns with NULL. The last printed row has an empty score because the SQLite CLI displays NULL as empty by default.
lessons.example:
WITH
  topic(id, title) AS (VALUES (1, 'Arrays'), (2, 'Loops')),
  attempt(topic_id, score) AS (VALUES (1, 8), (1, 10))
SELECT topic.title, attempt.score
FROM topic
LEFT JOIN attempt ON attempt.topic_id = topic.id
ORDER BY topic.id, attempt.score;

api.name: JOIN ... ON ...
api.description: Combine matching rows from two inputs.

api.name: LEFT JOIN ... ON ...
api.description: Keep unmatched left rows as well as matches.

api.name: REFERENCES parent(id)
api.description: Declare a foreign-key relationship. Enable PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON on each SQLite connection.

lessons.practice: Add an attempt for Loops and observe how the unmatched row changes.
lessons.pitfall: A WHERE filter on a right-table field can remove the NULL rows that a left join preserved.

exercise.expected: Include topics with and without attempts.
exercise.completion: Two attempts produce two joined rows, and an unmatched topic still appears once.

lessons.title: Grouping, aggregates, and HAVING
lessons.explanation: An aggregate combines a group of rows into a result. WHERE filters individual rows before grouping. HAVING filters the groups produced by GROUP BY.
lessons.example:
WITH attempt(topic, points) AS (
    VALUES ('Arrays', 8), ('Arrays', 10), ('Loops', 6), ('Loops', NULL)
)
SELECT topic, COUNT(points) AS graded, AVG(points) AS average
FROM attempt
GROUP BY topic
HAVING AVG(points) >= 8
ORDER BY average DESC;

api.name: COUNT(*)
api.description: Count every row in the group.

api.name: COUNT(column)
api.description: Count non-NULL values in that column.

api.name: SUM() / AVG()
api.description: Calculate a sum or average over non-NULL inputs.

api.name: HAVING condition
api.description: Filter grouped results.

lessons.practice: Display total attempts and graded attempts side by side, including the group with a missing score.
lessons.pitfall: Averages are computed from non-NULL values. Treating a missing value as zero changes the result.

exercise.expected: Report both total and graded attempts for all topics.
exercise.completion: A NULL score contributes to COUNT(*) and not COUNT(points).

lessons.title: Updates, transactions, and parameters
lessons.explanation: Use transactions to group writes so they commit together. ROLLBACK discards changes from the current transaction. Application code should bind input values through parameters.

api.name: UPDATE ... SET ... WHERE ...
api.description: Change fields in selected rows.

api.name: DELETE FROM ... WHERE ...
api.description: Remove selected rows.

api.name: BEGIN / COMMIT / ROLLBACK
api.description: Start, save, or abandon a transaction.

api.name: WHERE id = ?
api.description: Use a parameter placeholder and bind it through your SQLite client.

lessons.practice: Replace COMMIT with ROLLBACK. Compare the final scores.
lessons.pitfall: An UPDATE or DELETE without WHERE targets every row. Preview the predicate with SELECT first.

exercise.expected: Compare the committed example with a rolled-back update.
exercise.completion: After rollback both scores have their original values.

lessons.title: Indexes and query plans
lessons.explanation: An index helps SQLite find rows without scanning the full table for some query shapes. Indexes occupy space and make writes more expensive. Examine the plan for the query you actually run. Look for note_category in the query plan and Joins in the result. Query plan formatting varies by SQLite version.

api.name: CREATE INDEX name ON table(column)
api.description: Maintain a lookup structure for a column.

api.name: EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN SELECT ...
api.description: Inspect SQLite’s high-level execution strategy.

api.name: ANALYZE
api.description: Collect statistics the query planner can use.

lessons.practice: Try a query on title alone. Compare its plan before and after adding a title index.
lessons.pitfall: An index need not be used. The optimizer chooses a plan based on available indexes and the query.

exercise.expected: Compare the plan for a filter before and after adding an index to its lookup column.
exercise.completion: Use the same query and check whether the plan reports the index.

lessons.title: Enforce valid relationships with foreign keys
lessons.explanation: A foreign key constrains an attempt to reference an existing topic. SQLite foreign-key enforcement is a connection setting, so turn it on explicitly for every connection, before starting a transaction.

api.name: PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON
api.description: Enable foreign-key checks for the current SQLite connection.

api.name: REFERENCES topic(id)
api.description: Name the parent key that must match.

lessons.practice: Try inserting an attempt for a nonexistent topic, then try a valid topic ID.
lessons.pitfall: Adding a REFERENCES declaration does not reliably turn enforcement on. Set it explicitly and verify it on each connection.

exercise.expected: The orphan attempt is rejected while the valid attempt succeeds.
exercise.completion: Run with enforcement on and check that deleting a parent with a remaining child also fails by default.

lessons.title: Calculate a running total without grouping away rows
lessons.explanation: A window function can compute a total while keeping one output row per input row. PARTITION BY resets the calculation for each topic. ORDER BY id within the window and an explicit ROWS frame give a cumulative total through the current row.

api.name: SUM(...) OVER (...)
api.description: Compute a sum across the rows in the current window frame.

api.name: PARTITION BY topic
api.description: Give each topic an independent running total.

lessons.practice: Add another Loops attempt and verify that each running total changes only for its own topic.
lessons.pitfall: Window order controls the calculation. Use an outer ORDER BY when the displayed row order matters too.

exercise.expected: The result still has one row per attempt, with a cumulative duration for the attempt’s topic.
exercise.completion: Try an interleaved topic order and one topic containing only a single attempt.
